methodology: Freeze exact 333 IDs, paths, source metadata, and original bytes before classification.
Retrieve the complete public pinned archive; parse all real recommendation GUIDs across three source roots and explicitly exclude archetype placeholders.
Read all frozen/current matched requirement narratives; classify primary intent with reviewed overrides instead of assigning APRL wholesale to Reliability.
Compare title, longDescription, impact, resource scope and corresponding KQL; retain unresolved scope/query differences and disabled guidance with explicit gaps.
Apply separately documented corrections from retrieved Microsoft Learn pages; only four upstream query changes received bounded static adoption, and four misleading queries were withdrawn.
Compare-and-swap preflight every frozen path before any replacement; preserve original identities/source/aliases/dates, and never write another source slice.
limitations: This is the complete pinned repository GUID denominator, not a count of recommendations endorsed for present deployment: 393 Active and 63 Disabled.
Six docs/archetypes placeholder records are excluded; real specialized-workload and WAF records are included.
Per-item hashes cover the stated metadata payload, not KQL. Query text, drift, and static review decisions are recorded separately.
Only the frozen 333 APRL-source corpus IDs are semantically assessed here. Unmapped upstream IDs may be covered by other owned corpus records; no absence claim is made about them.
Published APRL text is not automatically a correct service contract. Independently verified corrections and unresolved upstream contradictions are recorded per corpus ID.
No Azure queries or deployments were executed. Null execution/review dates are preserved; assessedAt records source assessment only.
Upstream metadata is distributed under the Microsoft MIT license; see adjacent aprl-upstream-license.txt and the pinned repository LICENSE.
Freshness is per item/payload, not a blanket lastReviewed stamp. Full means the assessed published metadata requirement is represented, not an independent service certification.
Most source-linked Learn articles were not independently fetched; only separately listed correction documents have independent document review.
The source's pgVerified flag is upstream metadata, not proof that this refresh ran a product-group or Azure validation.
